cards.explanation: The answer is Dagon. The Philistines carry the ark into the temple of Dagon and set it beside his statue (1 Samuel 5:2). Dagon was the god of Ashdod. Remember that spot, friends, because the next morning is something else.

The answer is Dagon fallen on his face before the ark. The people of Ashdod get up early and there is Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD (1 Samuel 5:3). Nobody mentions a storm or an earthquake. I think those folks rubbed their eyes and checked twice, because I would have.

The answer is False. The text says they took Dagon and returned him to his place (1 Samuel 5:3). Nobody left him on the floor. I think they dusted him off and hoped nobody saw, like a guy who trips on the sidewalk and keeps walking.

The answer is his head and hands are broken off. This time Dagon is on his face again, with his head and his hands broken off and lying on the threshold (1 Samuel 5:4). Only the torso remained. Standing him up one time was a nice try, friends, and the second morning was a whole different story.

The answer is True. The text says that to this day, the priests of Dagon and all who enter his temple in Ashdod do not step on the threshold (1 Samuel 5:5). That's where the head and hands were found lying. I think they remember it every time they walk in, and they step high.

The answer is LORD. The hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod and its vicinity, ravaging them and afflicting them with tumors (1 Samuel 5:6). Notice whose hand it is, friends. The text names the LORD.

The answer is that the ark must not stay with them. The men of Ashdod say, “The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us…” (1 Samuel 5:7). They tie it to what they've seen: His hand is heavy upon them and upon their god Dagon. That's their decision, friends.

The answer is Gath. The rulers answer, “It must be moved to Gath…” and the people carry the ark away (1 Samuel 5:8). Gath is another Philistine city. I think everybody in Ashdod was thrilled to pass this one down the road.

The answer is False. The text says the LORD's hand was against Gath, afflicting the men of the city, both young and old, with an outbreak of tumors (1 Samuel 5:9). It also threw the city into great confusion. Young and old alike, so no age group got to say, "Not me."

The answer is that the ark was brought to kill them. As the ark arrives, the Ekronites cry out, “They have brought us the ark of the God of Israel in order to kill us and our people!” (1 Samuel 5:10). The cry comes right as it arrives. I think Ekron was alarmed, friends.

The answer is True. The Ekronites call together all the rulers of the Philistines and say, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel. It must return to its place…” (1 Samuel 5:11). They add that they want it gone so it will not kill them and their people. That's their whole request, friends.

The answer is heaven. The outcry of the city went up to heaven (1 Samuel 5:12). Those who didn't die were afflicted with tumors. This is a heavy part of the story, friends, and I think the city was in real misery.
